what: Line-by-line review of the merged tree at f98b44d, with every claim checked against an official or named reference source and a link attached. A finding without a verified source is recorded as an OPEN QUESTION, never as a value.
method: Re-read the official page it cites.
Compare character by character where the value is a string or an integer.
If the official page cannot confirm it, leave it blank and flag it here.

findings.finding: The scheduled refresh could never rebuild. scripts/refresh_official.py invoked the gate with --manifest/--json-out, which scripts/freshness_gates.py does not accept (it takes --max-report-age-hours), so the call exited 2 with a usage error.
findings.evidence: `python3 scripts/freshness_gates.py --manifest x --json-out y` prints 'error: unrecognized arguments' and exits 2 (reproduced in this session). GitHub run 43742524756 failed in the fetch step with the later steps skipped.
findings.action: Fixed: the refresh names freshness_gates_round_79341829.py, which accepts those flags, and fails loudly on a usage error.

findings.finding: The gate was not between the fetch and the push. The workflow fetched in one step and committed+pushed to main in a later step, so a fetch that exited 0 could publish.
findings.evidence: Read of .github/workflows/refresh.yml before this round: separate 'Fetch' and 'Commit ... git push origin HEAD:main' steps.
findings.action: Fixed: fetch -> gates -> rebuild -> publication checks are one call whose non-zero exit blocks the commit; a test asserts the workflow has exactly two steps and one call into the pipeline.

findings.finding: The brief names the official standings page; the job never fetched it (only the three team-stat pages).
findings.evidence: No occurrence of nba.com/standings in refresh_official.py before this round.
findings.action: Fixed: STANDINGS is fetched into the manifest and covered by the manifest gate.

findings.finding: The projection site published travel distances as PLAUSIBLE NUMBERS while the travel table itself reported 0 of 44 team-games sourced. app/projections.html printed 'LAC: 0.0 km', 'PHX: … DEN: 1740.1 km', 'PHI: … ORL: 0.0 km' from data/app/estimators.json, while data/live/rest_travel.json simultaneously said travel_unverified: 44, status NOT POPULATED.
findings.evidence: Read of the committed tree at f98b44d. data/live/rest_travel.json counts {'travel_unverified': 44} of 44. app/projections.html prints numeric km for the same team-games. That is a contradiction inside one repository: one surface says the value is unverified, another prints it as a measurement. IMPORTANT correction to my own first draft of this finding: the 0.0 km values are NOT wrong. PHI, PHX and LAC each played at home in their previous game (verified against data/origin/games.csv: BOS@PHI 11/10 and TOR@PHI 11/12, CHA@PHX 11/12, OKC@LAC 11/13), so zero distance is the correct value. My first draft called them a defect; that was wrong and is corrected here.
findings.action: Fixed in the direction that matters: the coordinate table now exists, 44/44 priced-window team-games resolve to a sourced coordinate, and the whole window is 352/420 with the 68 blanks published with reasons. The old city-keyed resolver is disabled (venue_key raises) so it cannot be revived by accident, and its outputs are replaced by scripts/travel_distance.py. A separate change request (CR-42-07) asks the owner of scripts/estimators.py to stop printing its own travel numbers, because two sources for one number is how the contradiction arose.

findings.finding: Arena coordinates are not published by the NBA. The new table is sourced from the MediaWiki coordinates API, a reference source rather than an official one.
findings.evidence: No nba.com page read in this repository publishes latitude/longitude.
findings.action: Every distance carries source_tier=reference and the label 'REFERENCE, NOT OFFICIAL'. Two arenas whose old article titles returned no coordinates were re-queried under their current names and resolved (Xfinity Mobile Arena, Mortgage Matchup Center); the failing old title is kept in blank_venues rather than deleted.
findings.status: FLAGGED — reference source, labelled as such

findings.finding: Settlement could never run for a new game day: publish_picks.py read one hard-coded feed (11/14) and CI never called the settle path at all.
findings.evidence: `grep -n settle .github/workflows/pages.yml` returned nothing before this round.
findings.action: Fixed: every data/live/results/settled_*.json is read, a verified 11/15 final was captured from two agreeing official reads, and the ledger now holds one SETTLE entry with its stamp.

findings.finding: The first settlement this session wrote a stamp of 2026-11-15T12:10Z for a game that tipped at 18:00Z and ended after 20:30Z — a settlement time before its own game.
findings.evidence: Read of the SETTLE entry this session wrote, compared with the pick's own tip_et_iso.
findings.action: Fixed: settlement_stamp() takes the feed row's settled_utc (when the two official reads were taken) and refuses any stamp earlier than the end of the game day.

findings.finding: Only 1 of 9 games on 11/15 has a verified final. One pick (HOU @ WAS) has a game day that has ended with no verified final on disk.
findings.evidence: 8 of 9 games had no second official read (no game book captured) in this session.
findings.action: Published as outstanding, not graded, not hidden. The refresh job has to close it by capturing the game book.

findings.finding: No closing line exists in the repository, so the market-anchored prior is not applied and no edge can be claimed against a price.

findings.action: Unchanged. This is Q1 below: it needs a licensed feed, which is a decision, not a fetch.
